title: UEFA Champions League Officiating: VAR Protocols, Handballs & Offside Technology
workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology
description: Advanced sports English module investigating VAR intervention thresholds, semi-automated offside technology (SAOT), unnatural silhouette handball rules, and on-field review (OFR) communication.
grammar_focus: Past Modals of Deduction & Forensic Review
learning_objectives: Master IFAB Laws of the Game terminology (clear and obvious error, on-field review, unnatural silhouette, subjective decision)
Apply past modals of deduction (must have, couldn't have, should have) to contentious refereeing replays
Demonstrate precision in forensic video review dialogue and match official protocols

questions.prompt: The VAR room _____ intervened on the soft penalty call because the on-field decision did not constitute a 'clear and obvious error'.

explanations.correct: Negative past modal 'couldn't have' correctly expresses lack of regulatory authority under strict IFAB protocol.
explanations.wrong_B: 'must not to have' is ungrammatical syntax.
explanations.wrong_C: 'shouldn't of' is a common colloquial spelling mistake for 'shouldn't have'.
explanations.wrong_D: 'might not have to' distorts the meaning of retrospective protocol compliance.

questions.cz_learning_point: Pro vyjádření nemožnosti nebo nepřípustnosti v minulosti použijte 'couldn't have + příčestí': 'couldn't have intervened'.
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: If the defender _____ his arm tucked firmly against his torso, the referee would not have penalized him for handball.

explanations.correct: Third conditional requires Past Perfect ('had kept') in the if-clause to discuss an unreal past incident.
explanations.wrong_B: Cannot use 'would have' inside the condition if-clause.
explanations.wrong_C: Past Simple 'kept' forms a Second Conditional, which mismatches past result 'would not have penalized'.
explanations.wrong_D: Present Perfect 'has kept' cannot be used in counterfactual past conditions.

questions.cz_learning_point: Třetí kondicionál (minulá nereálná situace) vyžaduje v 'if' větě předminulý čas: 'If the defender had kept... he would not have...'.
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: It _____ by UEFA officiating directors that semi-automated offside technology virtually eliminates human optical error.

explanations.correct: Passive reporting structure 'It is widely acknowledged that...' establishes authoritative executive consensus.
explanations.wrong_B: Active voice lacks a human subject.
explanations.wrong_C: Continuous form fails to express an established institutional stance.

questions.cz_learning_point: Formální pasivní vazba 'It is widely acknowledged that...' (Všeobecně se uznává, že...) je typická pro oficiální protokoly.
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: Under IFAB regulations, the match referee _____ carry out an on-field review (OFR) for any subjective red-card incident.

explanations.correct: Deontic modal 'shall' denotes mandatory regulatory obligation in official sports governing rules.
explanations.wrong_B: 'might' denotes weak possibility rather than mandatory directive.
explanations.wrong_C: 'ought' requires 'to' ('ought to') and conveys moral recommendation rather than strict statute.
explanations.wrong_D: 'is able to' denotes physical capability, not legal obligation.

questions.cz_learning_point: V oficiálních pravidlech IFAB a předpisech UEFA vyjadřuje závaznou povinnost právní způsobové sloveso 'shall' (musí / je povinen).
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: Rarely _____ a referee overturn an on-field offside ruling without consulting the synchronized calibrated crosshair freeze-frame.

explanations.correct: Inversion after negative adverbial 'Rarely' requires auxiliary 'does' before subject 'a referee'.
explanations.wrong_B: 'is' cannot invert with dynamic bare verb 'overturn'.
explanations.wrong_C: 'will' creates an unnatural predictive statement rather than habitual officiating standard.

questions.cz_learning_point: Po záporných a omezujících příslovcích na začátku věty (Rarely, Seldom, Never) dochází k inverzi (pomocné sloveso + podmět): 'Rarely does a referee overturn...'.
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: If the attacker _____ offside during the early phase of the build-up, the winning goal would stand on the scoreboard right now.

explanations.correct: Mixed conditional requires Past Perfect ('had not strayed') in the if-clause with present result ('would stand right now').
explanations.wrong_B: 'did not stray' is Simple Past, failing to denote past completion before present match outcome.
explanations.wrong_D: Present Perfect cannot express counterfactual past hypotheses.

questions.cz_learning_point: Smíšený kondicionál (minulá akce s následkem v přítomnosti) vyžaduje v 'if' větě předminulý čas: 'If the attacker had not strayed... the goal would stand now'.
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: The UEFA Chief of Refereeing recommended that referees _____ yellow cards immediately to players demonstrating excessive dissent.

explanations.correct: Subjunctive mood after verbs of recommendation ('recommended that referees issue') takes the base form.
explanations.wrong_B: Indicative past 'issued' is informal in formal regulatory mandates.
explanations.wrong_C: 'will issue' is incorrect in formal subjunctive clauses.
explanations.wrong_D: Continuous 'are issuing' violates formal directive syntax.

questions.cz_learning_point: Po slovesech doporučení a nařízení (recommend, demand, require that) se ve formální angličtině používá konjunktiv (base form): 'recommended that referees issue'.
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: It was the defender's unnatural body silhouette _____ convinced the match official to award the stoppage-time spot kick.

explanations.correct: Cleft sentence structure 'It was [X] that [verb]' emphasizes the decisive factor.
explanations.wrong_B: 'what' is a common Czenglish error (*It was X what convinced*).
explanations.wrong_C: 'whose' is possessive and cannot link a nominal clause here.

questions.cz_learning_point: Vytýkací věta (cleft sentence) pro zdůraznění příčiny vyžaduje vazbu 'It was [something] that...': 'It was the silhouette that convinced the official' (nikoli *what*).
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: _____ the multi-angle synchronized ultra-slow-motion footage, the lead official signaled for an offside restart.

explanations.correct: Perfect participle clause 'Having reviewed' concisely indicates that the video assessment was completed before the whistle.
explanations.wrong_B: Past participle 'Reviewed' would make the official the recipient of the review.
explanations.wrong_D: 'After to review' is completely incorrect phrasing.

questions.cz_learning_point: Minulé příčestí (perfect participle) 'Having reviewed...' (Poté, co přezkoumal záznam...) vyjadřuje ukončený předcházející děj.
questions.workplace_track: World Sports: Match Officiating & VAR Technology

questions.prompt: The disciplinary committee sanctioned the manager _____ accordance with Law 5 of the IFAB regulations.

explanations.correct: Fixed prepositional phrase is 'in accordance with' (v souladu s).
explanations.wrong_C: 'under of' is an invalid hybrid preposition.

questions.cz_learning_point: Ustálená formální právní předložková vazba je 'in accordance with' (v souladu s pravidly).
